plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: In the Southern Hemisphere's late spring, streets glow with clouds of trumpet-shaped lilac-blue flowers. Fallen blossoms carpet the pavement in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (roughly October to December)
plants.location: Eastern Australia, including Brisbane and Sydney
plants.funFact: Jacaranda trees are native to South America. In Australia, the trees' flowering is traditionally linked with university exam season.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In the wild, poinsettia grows as a tall shrub or small tree. Its fiery bracts flare out around tiny yellow flowers. Those bracts are the colorful part most people mistake for petals.
plants.location: Native forests of southern Mexico and Central America
plants.funFact: The showy red parts are modified leaves called bracts. The true flowers are the tiny yellow clusters at their center.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens delicate, fragrant blooms when most garden plants are fading. Its flowers brighten cool days in the northern hemisphere's late autumn and early winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Gardens in Japan, the southeastern United States and other mild-winter regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is native to Japan. It is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Round heads of trumpet-shaped blue flowers rise on tall, slender stems above strappy green leaves. They put on a cheerful summer show in gardens and along roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (about November to January in Western Australia)
plants.location: Gardens in Western Australia and its native South Africa
plants.funFact: Despite the name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. The name comes from Greek words meaning love flower.
